size_note: about $1B notional short plus long-dated puts
pnl_note: covered Feb 2018 after ~5 years; stock well above 2012 entry; estimated loss near $1B
why_what: Ackman argued Herbalife was a pyramid scheme regulators would shut down. The 2016 FTC settlement fined the company but did not close it, and Carl Icahn's large long kept pressure on shorts.
how: $1B public short promoted with a 342-slide presentation in Dec 2012; later swapped some exposure into put options.
where_ctx: Played out in public: activist presentations, a CNBC brawl with Icahn, years of SEC filings; exit announced Feb 2018.
lesson: A short thesis that depends on regulator action is not under your control; unlimited-loss shorts need a catalyst you own.

market: US equities hedged via CDS indices
pnl_note: about $2.6B gain in under a month; exited Mar 23-25, 2020
why_what: Ackman judged in late Feb 2020 that COVID would shut the US economy while credit spreads priced almost no risk.
how: Bought CDS protection on investment-grade and high-yield indices; sold after spreads blew out and redeployed into beaten-down stocks (Hilton, Restaurant Brands).
where_ctx: Disclosed in Pershing Square investor letters and a CNBC interview while the hedge was on.
lesson: Asymmetric convexity trades (small premium, huge payout) work best when tail risk is mispriced; exit into the panic, don't marry the hedge.

pnl_note: roughly $1.6-2B profit; exited June 2015
why_what: Icahn bought in 2012 when the market punished the Qwikster era, arguing streaming made Netflix undervalued and a takeover target.
how: Common stock disclosed via 13D in late 2012; held through the streaming growth ramp; sold the last shares June 2015.
where_ctx: Tracked through SEC filings; exit announced on Twitter and covered same day.
lesson: Buying a platform transition the market hates, then holding through the ramp, beats trading around the story.

size_note: Scion position near $3-4 per share in 2019
pnl_note: exited by Q4 2020, reportedly ~$100M gain, before the Jan 2021 squeeze peak
why_what: Deep value case: net cash, viable core business, and buybacks that could retire stock far below intrinsic value; Burry also flagged >100% short interest as fuel.
how: Common stock plus activist letters urging a $238M buyback; disclosed via 13D filings.
where_ctx: Letters published Aug 2019; SC 13D filings track the build and exit.
lesson: Cash-backed value plus a buyback catalyst can precede a squeeze; you do not need to hold for the blow-off top to win big.

pnl_note: about -53% of fund in Jan 2021 (~$4.5B) despite a $2.75B Citadel/Point72 infusion
why_what: Melvin held a big GME short into a coordinated retail squeeze; short interest above float made covering brutally expensive.
how: Short forced closed at extreme prices during the WallStreetBets squeeze; told clients it exited Jan 27, 2021.
where_ctx: Loss first reported by WSJ, confirmed to CNBC.
lesson: When short interest exceeds float, position size becomes the risk; crowding, not thesis quality, kills you.

size_note: large concentrated long with board seats
pnl_note: sold entire stake Mar 2017; loss about $3-4B
why_what: Backed a roll-up built on acquisitions and price hikes; the Philidor pharmacy scandal and price-gouging probes destroyed the model; stock fell >90%.
how: Concentrated long, doubled down through 2015-2016 instead of cutting early.
where_ctx: Tracked via 13Fs, congressional hearings, and the Mar 2017 sale release.
lesson: Doubling down on a broken business model turns a bad trade into a catastrophic one; concentration needs a stop on thesis, not just price.

pnl_note: GMCR fell ~50% within weeks of the Oct 2011 presentation and kept sliding into 2012
why_what: The 'GAAP-uccino' deck attacked aggressive accounting, weak K-Cup margin disclosure, expiring patents and insider selling.
how: Public short thesis at the Value Investing Congress, 110-slide presentation; confirmed on CNBC.
where_ctx: Conference presentation plus press coverage.
lesson: Detailed public forensic work on accounting quality can be the catalyst itself for an overvalued momentum stock.

pnl_note: shorted from the $70-90 area down toward the Dec 2001 bankruptcy
why_what: Chanos read Enron's own filings: single-digit return on capital, executives cashing out, CFO-run off-balance-sheet entities.
how: Straight short on the common, sized up as evidence mounted; shared the thesis with journalist Bethany McLean.
where_ctx: Flagged publicly late 2000; Fortune story 'Is Enron Overpriced?' ran Mar 2001.
lesson: The filings often contain the fraud; low return on capital in a 'great' company is a red flag worth acting on.

instrument: CDS on subprime MBS / ABX indices
pnl_note: Paulson & Co made ~$15B in 2007; Paulson personally ~$4B
why_what: Paulson and Pellegrini concluded subprime loans were built to default once teaser rates reset, and CDS priced default risk near zero.
how: Bought credit default swaps on subprime bonds and ABX indices and held through 2007.
where_ctx: Documented by the WSJ and Zuckerman's 'The Greatest Trade Ever'.
lesson: When the insurance on a systemic risk is cheap, the asymmetry can be career-defining; conviction plus structure beats timing.

pnl_note: stake worth >$160B at early-2022 peak; >$120B unrealized profit
why_what: Buffett reframed Apple as a consumer-products company with extreme loyalty and huge buybacks, not a tech stock.
how: Accumulated common stock 2016-2018 (started by deputies Combs/Weschler), then held while buybacks raised Berkshire's share.
where_ctx: Build and holding tracked through Berkshire 13Fs and annual letters.
lesson: Reframe the business correctly and position size plus time do the compounding; buybacks amplify a static stake.

pnl_note: sold entire position in four airlines in Apr 2020 at a loss Buffett called a mistake
why_what: Thesis was that consolidation had fixed industry economics; COVID broke cash flows and Buffett judged recovery would take years with dilutive bailouts.
how: Common-stock positions exited in the open market during Apr 2020.
where_ctx: Disclosed at the May 2, 2020 annual meeting; Buffett: 'I made a mistake'.
lesson: When the thesis dies, exit fully rather than averaging; even Buffett cuts losers.

pnl_note: -26.4% on Feb 3, 2022, erasing ~$251B; largest one-day value loss in market history at the time
why_what: Q4 2021 showed first-ever daily-active-user decline, weak guidance, ~$10B hit from Apple's ad-tracking changes and accelerating metaverse losses.
how: Earnings gap down; holders had no exit between the close and the open.
where_ctx: Earnings after the Feb 2 close; record loss widely reported Feb 3.
lesson: Earnings gaps bypass stops; sizing for gap risk matters more than stop placement for event holding.

size_note: ~$50B of value erased in one day
pnl_note: about -35% on Apr 20, 2022, worst day since 2004
why_what: First subscriber loss in a decade (-200k) and guidance for -2M more broke the growth story behind the multiple.
how: Earnings gap down after the Apr 19 close.
where_ctx: Q1 2022 earnings; covered same day by CNBC, WSJ, BBC.
lesson: When the story is 'growth forever', the first miss on the core metric re-rates everything at once.

pnl_note: +155% (1997 USIC win) and +334.8% (2021 win, stock-division record)
why_what: Momentum/swing method (SEPA): trade stocks with accelerating earnings and strong relative strength, tight risk per trade, press winners in favorable cycles.
how: Concentrated swing trading in high-relative-strength US stocks; results verified against brokerage statements per contest rules.
where_ctx: US Investing Championship standings published by the organizer; 2021 win via press release.
lesson: Documented repeat wins over 24 years show the edge is the risk framework (cut fast, press strength), not one hot market.

pnl_note: +941% in the 2020 USIC stock division
why_what: Rode the post-COVID momentum cycle: bought leaders on base breakouts after the Mar 2020 crash and pyramided winners through the uptrend.
how: Swing trading on the 'cycle of price action': accumulation, markup, distribution, decline; tight stops, sizing into strength.
where_ctx: Final standings on Business Wire; method described in later interviews.
lesson: Cycle-aware trading means maximum aggression only in the markup phase; the same style loses in distribution.

size_note: started with about $53,000 in calls and shares
pnl_note: screenshots showed ~$48M at the Jan 2021 peak; realized P&L never audited
why_what: Gill's public thesis: GME undervalued versus its cash, console cycle plus Ryan Cohen could re-rate it, and >100% short interest made a squeeze possible.
how: Long-dated call options plus shares, built from mid-2019, documented in YouTube videos and daily Reddit posts.
where_ctx: Posted as u/DeepFuckingValue on r/wallstreetbets; testified under oath to Congress Feb 18, 2021.
lesson: Options turned a small deep-value stake into life-changing convexity, but only the documented thesis (not the screenshots) is verifiable.

pnl_note: ~$5,000 grew to ~$22M over 50 years; left to Yeshiva University
why_what: Extreme compounding: reinvested dividends in quality companies and never sold, living frugally on a small pension.
how: Buy and hold with dividend reinvestment across five decades, no leverage, no trading.
where_ctx: Estate documented after her 1995 death; Money magazine reviewed the broker statements.
lesson: Time in the market with reinvested dividends can beat nearly every active approach; behavior is the edge.

pnl_note: $180 became ~$7M by 2010, donated to Lake Forest College
why_what: 75 years of holding one employer's stock with dividends reinvested; splits and compounding did the work.
how: Bought 3 Abbott shares in 1935, reinvested every dividend, never sold.
where_ctx: Confirmed by Lake Forest College and her estate; covered widely in 2010.
lesson: Single-stock compounding works spectacularly when the company survives and you never interrupt it; it is also undiversifiable luck.

instrument: dividend-paying blue chips (J&J, P&G, railroads, banks)
size_note: modest savings from gas-station and janitor wages
pnl_note: ~$8M portfolio at death in 2014; $6M to a local library and hospital
why_what: Frugal living plus steady buying of dividend payers, paper certificates held for decades.
how: Buy and hold, dividends reinvested or saved, no leverage.
where_ctx: Estate revealed at his 2014 death; holdings verified via his broker and the bequests.
lesson: Consistency and decades of compounding beat sophistication; the method was boring on purpose.

market: US equities via total return swaps
pnl_note: family office wiped out; prime brokers lost >$10B (Credit Suisse ~$5.5B, Nomura ~$2.9B)
why_what: Hwang ran extreme leverage through swaps at several banks, hiding true position size; a ViacomCBS offering triggered declines that forced margin calls and fire sales.
how: Concentrated leveraged long exposure via total return swaps, no direct ownership on file.
where_ctx: Collapse in the week of Mar 22-26, 2021; bank losses disclosed in Q1 2021 earnings.
lesson: Hidden leverage plus concentration means the margin call, not the thesis, decides the exit; swaps remove the disclosure that would warn others.

pnl_note: Greenlight's biggest loser of 2020; fund returned ~5% in a year TSLA rose 743%
why_what: Einhorn called Tesla a bubble propped up by promotion and questionable accounting; the market kept paying for growth and S&P 500 inclusion forced index buying.
how: Short common stock, defended publicly in investor letters and a Twitter feud with Musk.
where_ctx: Losses disclosed in Greenlight quarterly letters, covered by Reuters.
lesson: Shorting a story stock on valuation alone fights reflexivity and index flows; the market can stay irrational longer than a short can stay solvent.

size_note: up to ~21% of the company, with board seats
pnl_note: estimated profit around $1B; sold >half back to the company for $600M in Jan 2021, fully out by May 2021
why_what: Icahn took the other side of Ackman's short, betting the FTC would not shut Herbalife and a short squeeze would reward longs.
how: Common stock position built after Ackman's 2012 presentation; reduced via negotiated buybacks.
where_ctx: Tracked in 13D filings; Jan 2021 $600M repurchase announced by Herbalife.
lesson: Being the liquidity on the other side of a crowded public short can be the trade itself.

size_note: concentrated Daily Journal position, partly on margin
pnl_note: halved the stake in Q1 2022 after the stock fell 50%+ from purchases; large loss crystallized
why_what: Bought into the 2020-2021 decline as a value play on Chinese e-commerce; regulatory crackdowns, ADR delisting risk and slowdown deepened the drawdown.
how: Concentrated common-stock position, cut in Apr 2022.
where_ctx: Visible in Daily Journal 13Fs; Munger later called Alibaba one of his worst mistakes.
lesson: Jurisdiction and regulation are part of the thesis; catching a falling knife with margin makes the cut forced, not chosen.

pnl_note: covered Apr 2020 after Luckin fell ~70% in one day (~90% from highs)
why_what: Chanos and others, helped by the anonymous Muddy Waters report, concluded same-store sales were fabricated; the company later admitted ~$310M of fake sales.
how: Short the ADR; covered into the April 2, 2020 collapse.
where_ctx: Chanos confirmed the cover on CNBC the day of the plunge.
lesson: Forensic short research on data you can independently check (store traffic, receipts) beats relying on reported numbers.

pnl_note: sold in Aug 2022 for about $58-68M profit; BBBY fell ~40% after his exit and later went bankrupt
why_what: Cohen disclosed an activist stake in Mar 2022 and pushed for strategic changes; meme traders ran the stock up again in Aug 2022, giving him an exit into strength.
how: Common stock plus options, disclosed via 13D; sold the entire position days after a new SEC filing showed intent to sell.
where_ctx: Exit confirmed in SEC filings Aug 17-18, 2022; stock tanked on the news.
lesson: Selling into a meme-driven squeeze is the point of activist optionality; followers who held his exit bag lost most of it.

size_note: mutual fund, tens of billions AUM at peak
pnl_note: Value Trust fell ~55% in 2008, erasing years of outperformance; the 15-year S&P-beating streak (1991-2005) ended badly
why_what: Miller concentrated in financials (AIG, Freddie Mac, Bear Stearns) as 'value' during the crisis; the cheap stocks were cheap because the businesses were insolvent.
how: Value-style concentrated long positions held through the 2008 crash.
where_ctx: Documented by the NYT and business press through 2008-2009.
lesson: A long streak can hide a single factor bet; value in leverage (banks) is a different risk than value in assets.

pnl_note: closed Tiger in Mar 2000 after ~19% drop in early 2000 and heavy redemptions, weeks before the Nasdaq peaked
why_what: Robertson refused to buy dot-com stocks, shorted the bubble too early, and redemptions forced selling of the value longs he believed in.
how: Long old-economy value, short tech; client redemptions forced liquidation at the worst moment.
where_ctx: Announced Mar 30, 2000; Nasdaq peaked days earlier on Mar 10 and crashed over the next two years.
lesson: Being right about the bubble and surviving it are different problems; client-flow risk can force liquidation right before the payoff.

pnl_note: about +14% on Feb 4, 2022, the largest single-day market-value gain in US market history at the time
why_what: Q4 2021 earnings showed strong AWS growth, Prime price increases, and a Rivian stake gain, one day after Meta's record loss.
how: Earnings gap up after the Feb 3 close.
where_ctx: Record gain reported by Reuters the next day.
lesson: Mega-cap earnings gaps cut both ways; event risk is symmetrical around crowded prints.

pnl_note: stake worth ~$6-9B+ by 2021-2024; Berkshire trimmed from 2022 with billions in profit
why_what: Munger championed BYD's battery technology and Wang Chuanfu as a manager; Berkshire paid ~$230M in 2008 and simply held through enormous drawdowns.
how: Common-stock stake via Berkshire's MidAmerican arm; held 14 years before trimming.
where_ctx: Purchase announced Sep 2008; trims disclosed in HK filings from 2022.
lesson: Patience through 50%+ drawdowns only works when the underlying franchise keeps compounding; the Munger-network sourcing was the edge.

pnl_note: sold in 2007 for about $4B; profit ~$3.5B
why_what: Buffett bought PetroChina at roughly 3x earnings with a big dividend when Chinese SOEs were ignored; sold purely on valuation when price reached his estimate of value.
how: Common-stock H-shares, held ~5 years, exited in stages through Oct 2007.
where_ctx: Exit confirmed by Buffett to CNBC/FOX in Oct 2007; he said price, not Darfur politics, drove the sale.
lesson: Sell discipline on valuation (not headlines) locked the gain; the stock peaked right after he finished selling.

pnl_note: Scion returned roughly +489% net from inception to mid-2008, driven by the subprime short; investors were restricted from redeeming during the wait
why_what: Burry read thousands of actual mortgage bond prospectuses and found loan quality collapsed in 2005-2006 vintages while CDS on the bonds stayed cheap.
how: Bought CDS directly on specific BBB subprime bonds, endured ~2 years of mark-to-market pain and investor revolt before the payoff in 2007-2008.
where_ctx: Documented in Michael Lewis's 'The Big Short' and contemporary coverage.
lesson: Being early on a short looks like being wrong for years; lock up capital and temperament before the trade, not after.

size_note: aggregate short interest across all funds
pnl_note: short sellers lost about $38B mark-to-market in 2020 as TSLA rose ~743%
why_what: The crowded valuation short ignored S&P 500 inclusion (forced index buying), delivery growth, and retail momentum; losses were the largest for any short that year.
how: Short common stock across many funds; S3 Partners tracked the aggregate losses.
where_ctx: Year-end 2020 tally from S3 Partners data, reported by Bloomberg.
lesson: Aggregate short-loss data shows crowding itself is the risk metric; a 'right' valuation view can still be a career-ending trade.

size_note: ~$15B of market value lost in one day
pnl_note: -43% on May 24, 2022, Snap's worst day ever, below its IPO price; dragged ad-tech peers down with it
why_what: CEO warned mid-quarter that revenue and earnings would miss guidance, blaming macro deterioration 'faster than expected' after Apple's ad-tracking changes.
how: Mid-quarter guidance warning between earnings, gap down at the open.
where_ctx: Warning filed May 23, 2022; the plunge and peer contagion covered same day.
lesson: Mid-quarter warnings in ad-driven names signal sector-wide demand shifts; the first warning is rarely the last.

pnl_note: $15B Kraft Heinz writedown Feb 2019; Berkshire lost ~$4B in one day on the stock's ~27% plunge; Buffett admitted overpaying
why_what: 3G Capital's cost-cutting model could not offset shifting consumer tastes away from packaged foods; a $15B goodwill writedown and an SEC subpoena hit together.
how: Long-held concentrated common-stock position from the 2015 Heinz-Kraft merger.
where_ctx: Writedown disclosed Feb 21, 2019; Buffett's 'overpaid' admission on CNBC Feb 25, 2019.
lesson: Brand moats erode silently; cost-cutting is not a growth strategy, and even Berkshire's best deals can be overpaid.

pnl_note: down ~90% from the Oct 2020 peak by Nov 2022
why_what: Pandemic pull-forward of demand ended: growth collapsed from triple digits to single digits while the valuation still priced hyper-growth.
how: Slow bleed lower over two years rather than one gap; each earnings cut guidance further.
where_ctx: Peak in Oct 2020; the ~90% drawdown noted by Reuters in Nov 2022.
lesson: Pull-forward demand stocks rarely V-recover; a fading growth rate with a hyper-growth multiple is a multi-year short even without fraud.

pnl_note: down >92% within about a year of the Jan 2021 peak; fell below its IPO price in Jan 2022
why_what: Demand was pulled forward by lockdowns; as gyms reopened, orders collapsed, a treadmill recall hit, and the company slashed guidance while inventories piled up.
how: Steady decline with earnings gaps lower (Nov 2021, May 2022) as guidance was cut repeatedly.
where_ctx: Collapse documented through 2021-2022 earnings coverage.
lesson: When a product's demand spike is tied to a temporary condition, model the unwind first; guidance cuts compound instead of clearing.
